answer: To raise the cost of fake identities, each new account must lock non-transferable collateral that thaws only after a glacier-slow vesting schedule of many epochs, and must also solve an admission proof whose difficulty climbs with recent join velocity. Watchers treat a ripple of synchronized votes or cloned answer templates as one farm: every bond in that cluster is slashed and those keys lose grading rights. A nebula of disposable accounts therefore costs the attacker one full locked stake plus a harder proof per head, already more than one epoch's reward share before any payout unlocks.
